Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 38, English)
Beyond Bhoot-Pr et: Why Devtas Themselves Can Turn Against You, and What Actually Protects You

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn sangat satsang (~1hr26min) opening with an aura-checking pr ogr ess update (70%+ r ecovery acr oss 150 people thr ough diya alone), followed by an extended teaching — built thr ough a live, evolving case-study discussion — on why negativity isn't limited to bhoot-pr et, why even devtas can act against a person, and why only one's own guru and jaap pr ovide r eal pr otection.
1. Aura-Checking Pr ogr ess Update: 70%+ Recovery Through Diya Alone

1. Bhaiya opens with a progress report: over the past three days, aura-checking was completed for ar ound 150 people , and the results were shared with each of them individually . Mor e than 70% showed their negativity completely clear ed compared to the prior month's aura-checking — achieved, in the lar ge majority of cases, simply by lighting a diya (lamp) for their deity/guru at home , without any additional payment, separate ritual, or special hawan (only two or three individuals were specifically advised to arrange a separate hawan). 2. Bhaiya attributes this r esult entirely to his guru's grace , not to any special ef fort of his own, and becomes visibly emotional describing mentors' reports of members' improvement.
2. Two Live Testimonials Shar ed During the Session

1. Vishal Kashyap , on his first day joining, reported feeling Bajrangbali (Hanuman) in a "virat" (vast/cosmic) form — described by Bhaiya as a rare and fortunate experience for a newcomer . 2. A sangat member (Ankur Gupta) shared that he had been ill for five to six years, with pain present in nearly every part of his body , and had spent a lar ge sum on medical treatment with limited relief. After being told in a prior aura-checking session simply to offer diyas to Hanuman Ji Maharaj in Ram's name — without ever visiting the ashram in person — he reports r oughly 95%+ r elief in his body . Bhaiya highlights this as a clear example of remote, name-based devotion producing real results without any in-person visit or additional payment.
3. Why Ashaeiynn Deliberately Avoids Gr owth, Advertising, and Media Exposur e

1. Bhaiya states explicitly that the institute has no inter est in mass advertising or rapid gr owth — he describes declining repeated of fers for YouT ube interviews and media exposure, reasoning that expanding to reach unfamiliar new audiences risks neglecting the members already present and committed. 2. His stated philosophy: "don't lose what's yours chasing something new ," and "one who tends to their own r oots goes further." He frames his own capacity as limited and prefers to fully serve the members already in his care rather than stretch thin chasing scale.
4. Negativity Isn't Limited to Bhoot-Pr et — Every Level Can Act Against You

1. Bhaiya's central teaching for this session: bhoot, pr et, pishach, kinnar , yaksha-yakshini, apsara, yoginis, devi-devtas, saints/mahatmas, and even Indra and the planets (grahas) themselves can, at some point, act against a person. This is described as something everyone eventually experiences in some form, regardless of how minor or major . 2. What actually pr otects a person in that moment is their own mantra, their ishta (chosen deity), and their guru — described as the "shield" that stands between a person and whatever level of being turns against them at a given time.
5. The Army General and the Mango Tree: Why Even the Powerful React to Small Infractions

1. An illustrative analogy: even someone with enormous standing and reputation (an army general, known and respected everywhere) will react sharply if someone plants even a single mango tree on their private territory without permission — not because the fruit itself matters, but because territory and protocol matter to those who hold power . The same principle is said to apply to deities and their domains — every region, dimension, and shrine has its own presiding deities and protectors, along with entities who claim and defend that territory .
6. Each Deity Has Differ ent Preferences — "Right and Wrong" Is Deity- and Place-Specific

1. This teaching states that each deity has its own individual pr eferences — Ganesh Bhagwan's ideal of fering is laddu; Bholenath, Mata, and Hanuman Ji Maharaj each prefer something dif ferent; even one's own kul devta (family deity) has their own specific preferences. "Right" and "wr ong" conduct is ther efor e not universal — it is specific to the deity and specific to the shrine/location. 2. Example given: at a temple where of fering a chunari (a decorative scarf/veil) to the Mata (goddess) is customary , arriving without one and instead bringing something else (like laddu) can be treated locally as a lapse — even though this same "lapse" would mean nothing at a dif ferent shrine with dif ferent customs. 3. Bhaiya adds a historical nuance: these specific rules/customs at any given shrine were originally established because they mattered for the time and context in which the shrine's practices were set — but the underlying spiritual need today may actually be dif ferent, even as the old customs continue to be followed literally .
7. Why a Devotee Might Get "Beaten" Over a Minor Ritual Lapse — and a Key Caution

1. Bhaiya describes a common r eal pattern: visitors who fail to follow a shrine's specific customs (e.g., not bringing a chunari) can be actively afflicted by the doots (messengers) stationed ther e — even though, he explicitly notes, it's worth asking whether the presiding deity itself genuinely wants visitors "beaten" over something as minor as a decorative scarf. This is offer ed as a caution against assuming every doot's actions ar e directly sanctioned or even known by the deity they serve — doots may act on a narrow , literal instruction ("punish anyone who doesn't bring a chunari") without the deity's full awareness or personal involvement.
8. A Live, Evolving Case-Study Framework: Why Outcomes Differ So Widely

1. To illustrate these dynamics concr etely , Bhaiya builds a live, evolving case study with the sangat (using real sangat members, including "Ritesh" and "Harshit," as illustrative stand-ins) around a single scenario: two people visit a Mata temple, and neither of fers the customary chunari.

Case 1 — Both people suffer , with no r elief: 15. In this scenario, both visitors ar e afflicted equally by the temple's doots. Bhaiya's blunt explanation: neither person has any standing, pr otection, or "clout" in that spiritual court — they arrive with nothing to of fer beyond a basic request, and the doots treat them accordingly , exactly as low-ranking petitioners might be treated by any powerful, unfamiliar authority . 16. A supporting r eal-world observation offer ed: a well-dressed, evidently wealthy visitor arriving in fine clothes is typically treated gently and respectfully even at an ordinary shrine or by ordinary people, while an ordinary visitor without any such visible standing may be pushed around and dismissed — the same asymmetry , per this teaching, plays out at the astral level as well, unless a person has built their own genuine spiritual "standing" (dimension/ener gy) independent of material wealth. 17. The teaching's stated r esolution for this case is not to simply accept mistr eatment, but to build enough personal spiritual

capacity ("dimension") that even a temple's own priest or resident shakti would come forward r espectfully to meet the practitioner , rather than the practitioner needing to seek favor as an anonymous, low-status visitor .

Case 2 — One r ecovers quickly , one does not: 18. In this scenario, one visitor recovers by the next day while the other continues to suffer . The sangat's own guesses (of fered live) include: dif fering ener gy levels from personal jaap, dif fering family/ancestral protection (kul devta), a stronger connection to one's own guru, or an existing devta dosh specific to one person. Bhaiya affirms that the key factor is whether the person has some other , stronger protective shakti at home (a kul devta, a guru, or similar) that is capable of dir ectly overpowering the local temple doot and sending it away . 19. A crucial principle stated dir ectly: "jaap bina shakti ke sirf jaap hi hai" — jaap performed without an underlying protective shakti backing it is merely jaap, with no defensive power of its own. 20. A deeper caution follows: if the af flicted person keeps returning to the external temple for relief, pouring their own spiritual ener gy/attention into that external shrine repeatedly (while home-based protection is never replenished, since all their devotional ener gy is now directed outward), the home-based pr otective shakti will eventually be depleted fr om constant, unreplenished use. Eventually , exhausted and desperate, the person may fall entirely at the external temple priest's feet — at which point, per this teaching, that priest can effectively absorb and claim the person's home-based pr otective shakti for himself, redirecting their future devotion/service entirely toward his own temple, deepening the person's dependency rather than resolving it.

Case 3 — One person is personally unaffected while their family suffers instead: 21. In this scenario, one visitor experiences no personal effects at all, while members of their own family (spouse, mother , sister) become ill or troubled instead , prompting the unaf fected person to shuttle family members between doctors without success. Bhaiya explains this by intr oducing two distinct types of doots: 22. Type one — doots who inflict visible affliction specifically to compel devotion , eventually driving the person back to that shrine, sometimes only after years, to finally of fer genuine devotion and be released. This type is oriented toward eventually gaining a devotee, even through initial coercion. 23. Type two — doots who deliberately keep their target unawar e that anything is happening at all, quietly devastating a person's household (family health, finances, r elationships) without ever revealing themselves — compared to money silently draining from a bank account without the account holder's knowledge. This type is described as far mor e danger ous pr ecisely because the affected person feels no personal urgency to act , even while their family openly suf fers and repeatedly ur ges them to "do something." 24. Bhaiya explains why some individuals ar e specifically targeted this way rather than dir ectly: if the doot can tell that directly af flicting a particular person would produce no visible reaction or behavioral change (because that person is simply unaf fected/indif ferent), targeting their family instead is a mor e effective way to eventually for ce a r eaction , since the person's family relationships are what actually motivate them. 25. A further nuance offer ed on why some entrenched, "well-positioned" doots persist without consequence: an established doot who already receives regular of ferings/sustenance and holds a secure position has little personal risk in continuing to act this way — the human tar get simply loses out, while the doot's own position remains undisturbed. This is of fered as an uncomfortable but observed reality , not a moral endorsement.
9. Why Wealthy or Prominent People Seem Less Pr one to This Kind of Affliction

1. Bhaiya offers a r ough estimate: r oughly 90% of wealthy or prominent individuals experience comparatively smooth lives r elative to ordinary people, with only a small minority (r oughly 2 in 100) experiencing this kind of sever e affliction. When the sangat is asked why this might be, one member of fers a self-critical observation that ordinary people themselves often perform comparatively little regular worship/service — Bhaiya affirms this as cor e to the explanation: consistent devotional practice and service is itself a major protective factor , regardless of one's financial status.
10. The Real, Reliable Pr otection: Guru and Naam-Jaap Alone

1. This teaching's central practical conclusion: only two things r eliably pr otect a person thr ough all of this — one's guru, and one's own naam-jaap (name-r epetition practice). These are described as the only forces capable of standing up for a person even when devtas, grahas, or a being as powerful as Indra himself might act against them — since ordinary bhoot-pretlevel threats are described as comparatively minor by contrast.

2. The practical instruction that follows: a person must personally become spiritually awakened and self-r eliant — there is no external rescuer to fully depend on; regular jaap, and lighting a diya for one's guru/ishta at home, are described as suf ficient, without any need to travel anywhere or perform elaborate rituals.
1 1. Live Q&A: How to Handle Family Pr essure to Visit a Major Temple/Dham

1. A sangat member asked how to handle situations wher e family pr essure requires visiting a major temple or dham. Bhaiya's guidance: appr oach any shakti encounter ed there with your own guru specifically invoked as witness — using a simple formulation along the lines of, "Hey [deity], I, a servant of my guru [name], bow to you with my guru as witness." 2. If the shrine holds genuine shakti, it will r ecognize and bow to the practitioner's own guru-connection rather than the reverse — Bhaiya cautions strongly against being a "hero" at such places (i.e., approaching with arrogance or self-importance), noting that some sangat members who skipped this guru-invoking step in the past were themselves af flicted as a result. 3. Bhaiya shar es his own r ecent example: visiting the Bhimeshwar (Bhimashankar) Jyotirlinga and the garbhagriha (inner sanctum) there, he bowed while invoking his own guru as witness, and reports experiencing a clear physical sensation of shaktipat (ener gy transfer) as a result, later reinforced by a distinct cooling sensation passing a nearby Ram temple.
12. A Brief Live Aside: Recognition and Respect Are Often Tied to Known Standing

1. Bhaiya uses a brief live example (a sangat member's husband, a Brigadier , whose rank wasn't initially known to the gr oup) to illustrate a r elated point: recognition and deference are often extended once someone's actual standing/designation becomes known — paralleling how a shrine's resident shakti may only show deference once a visitor's own guru-connection and spiritual standing is properly invoked and made known, rather than assumed automatically .
13. A Brief Live Aside: Unusual Disturbance During Jaap

1. A sangat member reported that monkeys gather ed outside their window and cr eated a loud disturbance right as they began their mantra jaap for the session — noted as unusual, though not analyzed in depth during this session.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Negativity isn't limited to bhoot-pr et — bhoot, pret, pishach, kinnar , yaksha-yakshini, apsara, yoginis, devi-devtas, saints, and even Indra and the planets can, at some point, act against a person; only one's own mantra, ishta, and guru function as a reliable shield when this happens. Every deity has differ ent individual pr eferences, and "right and wr ong" conduct is specific to the deity and the shrine , not universal — a lapse at one shrine (e.g., not of fering a chunari) may mean nothing at another . A doot's actions ar en't necessarily fully sanctioned or known by the deity it serves — question whether a deity would genuinely want a visitor punished over a minor ritual lapse rather than assuming every af fliction is deliberate, sanctioned divine will. "Jaap without an underlying pr otective shakti is just jaap" — personal practice alone doesn't guarantee protection without some backing force (a kul devta, a guru, or similar). Redirecting all devotional energy toward an external shrine while neglecting home-based pr otection can deplete that home pr otection over time, risking a dependency where an external priest eventually absorbs the person's home-based shakti and devotion entirely . Two types of afflicting doots exist: those who inflict visible af fliction specifically to eventually compel devotion, and those who quietly devastate a household without ever revealing themselves — the second type is more dangerous because the affected person feels no personal ur gency to act even as their family suf fers. Wealthy/pr ominent people ar e statistically less pr one to this kind of affliction (r oughly 90% r eport smoother lives) — partly attributed to more consistent worship/service, not merely financial status.

Only two things r eliably pr otect a person: one's guru, and one's own naam-jaap. No external rescuer can be fully depended on — becoming personally awakened and spiritually self-reliant is the only durable path. When visiting any temple or shakti under family pr essure, invoke your own guru as witness befor e bowing ("I, a servant of my guru, bow to you with my guru as witness") — a genuine shakti will recognize and defer to this rather than the reverse; never approach as a "hero" or with arrogance. Aura-checking acr oss r oughly 150 people showed 70%+ r ecovering fully thr ough nothing mor e than lighting a diya at home — no separate payment, ritual, or in-person visit required in most cases. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 38, English)
Beyond Bhoot-Pr et: Why Devtas Themselves Can Turn Against You, and What Actually Protects You
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live sangat satsang. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. What per centage of people showed impr ovement in the institute's r ecent aura-checking r ound, and how? A: Per this teaching, of roughly 150 people checked over three days, more than 70% showed their negativity completely cleared compared to the prior month — achieved in the lar ge majority of cases simply by lighting a diya for their deity/guru at home, with no separate payment or additional ritual required.

Q2. Is it necessary to visit the ashram in person to see r eal r esults? A: No — per this teaching, one member's account describes 5-6 years of illness improving by roughly 95%+ simply through of fering diyas to Hanuman Ji Maharaj in Ram's name, from home, without ever visiting in person.

Q3. Why doesn't Ashaeiynn actively advertise or seek media exposur e/interviews? A: Per this teaching, the institute deliberately avoids rapid growth or mass exposure, reasoning that expanding to reach unfamiliar new audiences risks neglecting the members already present and committed — the stated philosophy is "don't lose what's yours chasing something new ."

Q4. Is negativity only about bhoot-pr et (ghosts and low spirits)? A: No — per this teaching, bhoot, pret, pishach, kinnar , yakshayakshini, apsara, yoginis, devi-devtas, saints/mahatmas, and even Indra and the planets can, at some point, act against a person; this is described as something everyone eventually experiences in some form.

Q5. If even devtas can act against me, what actually pr otects a person in that situation? A: Per this teaching, only one's own mantra, ishta (chosen deity), and guru function as a reliable shield — these are described as standing between a person and whatever level of being turns against them at a given time.

Q6. Why would even powerful beings r eact sharply to something as small as a minor territorial infraction? A: This teaching uses an analogy of an army general reacting sharply if someone plants even a single mango tree on his private territory without permission — not because the fruit matters, but because territory and protocol matter to those who hold power; the same principle is said to apply to deities and their domains.

Q7. Does every deity have the same likes, dislikes, and rules? A: No — per this teaching, each deity has individual preferences (Ganesh prefers laddu, others prefer dif ferent of ferings), so "right and wrong" conduct is specific to the deity and the specific shrine/location, not universal.

Q8. If I don't follow a specific shrine's customs (like offering a chunari) and get afflicted by that shrine's doots, does that mean the deity itself wanted me punished? A: Not necessarily , per this teaching — Bhaiya explicitly raises the question of whether a deity would genuinely want a visitor "beaten" over something as minor as a decorative scarf, cautioning that a doot's actions aren't necessarily fully known or sanctioned by the deity it serves.

Q9. If two people both skip a shrine's ritual custom and both get afflicted with no r elief, why? A: Per this teaching, in this scenario, neither person has any spiritual "standing" or protection in that particular court — much like an anonymous, low-status visitor might be treated dismissively by any unfamiliar authority , while a person with recognizable "standing" is treated more gently .

Q10. What actually determines whether someone r ecovers quickly fr om this kind of affliction? A: Per this teaching, the key factor is whether the person has some other , stronger protective shakti at home — a kul devta, a guru, or a similar force capable of directly overpowering the local af fliction and removing it. As this teaching states directly: "jaap without an underlying protective shakti is just jaap."

Q1 1. Is it risky to keep r eturning to an external temple for relief instead of r elying on home-based practice? A: Yes, per this teaching — constantly redirecting devotional ener gy outward without replenishing home-based protection can eventually deplete that home protection, risking a dependency where the external temple's priest eventually absorbs and claims the person's home-based shakti and future devotion for himself.

Q12. Why might one family member seem personally unaffected by an affliction while the r est of the family suffers instead? A: Per this teaching, this reflects a specific type of doot that deliberately tar gets a person's family instead of the person directly — precisely because directly af flicting an indif ferent, unaf fected person wouldn't produce any reaction, while af fecting their family does.

Q13. What ar e the two types of afflicting doots described in this teaching? A: One type inflicts visible af fliction specifically to eventually compel the person back into devotion, sometimes after years, before releasing them. The second type deliberately keeps the person unaware anything is happening at all, quietly devastating their household — compared to money silently draining from a bank account — which this teaching describes as more dangerous, since the af fected person feels no personal ur gency to act even as their family suf fers.

Q14. Do doots that cause this kind of harm ever face any consequence for it? A: Not necessarily in the short term, per this teaching — an established doot who already holds a secure position and regular of ferings has little personal risk in continuing to act this way; this is presented as an uncomfortable observed reality rather than a moral endorsement.

Q15. Why do wealthy or prominent people seem to experience fewer of these pr oblems? A: Per this teaching, roughly 90% of wealthy or prominent individuals are estimated to have comparatively smooth lives, and this is attributed significantly to more consistent devotional practice and service — not simply to their financial status.

Q16. What ar e the only two things that r eliably pr otect a person against devtas, grahas, or even a being as powerful as Indra? A: Per this teaching, only one's guru and one's own naam-jaap (name-repetition practice) reliably protect a person through this — there is no external rescuer to fully depend on, and becoming personally spiritually awakened and self-reliant is presented as the only durable path.

Q17. My family pr essures me to visit big temples/dhams even though I've committed to home-based practice her e — what should I do? A: Per this teaching, when visiting any temple or shakti under family pressure, invoke your own guru specifically as witness before bowing (e.g., "I, a servant of my guru, bow to you with my guru as witness"). A genuine shakti will recognize and defer to this guru-connection rather than the reverse — never approach as a "hero" or with arrogance, since some sangat members who skipped this step were themselves af flicted.

Q18. Did Bhaiya himself use this guru-invoking practice r ecently? A: Yes — per this teaching, Bhaiya describes visiting the Bhimeshwar (Bhimashankar) Jyotirlinga's inner sanctum, bowing while invoking his own guru as witness, and experiencing a clear physical sensation of shaktipat as a result.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 38 additions)

When citing the 70%+ aura-checking recovery statistic or any specific testimonial (Ankur Gupta, Vishal Kashyap), present these as this teaching's own reported account, not as independently verified medical or spiritual outcomes — and never suggest these examples substitute for medical care. Preserve the core reframe that negativity spans all levels (bhoot-pret through devi-devtas, saints, Indra, and planets) — never let responses collapse this back into "negativity = only ghosts." When discussing why a doot might af flict someone over a minor ritual lapse, keep Bhaiya's own caution intact — that a doot's action isn't necessarily fully sanctioned by the deity it serves — rather than presenting every af fliction as deliberate divine will. Preserve the "jaap without shakti is just jaap" principle precisely when discussing personal protection — avoid implying that repetition alone, without a genuine protective backing, is suf ficient. When discussing the risk of over -relying on an external temple, keep the caution about home-based protection depletion intact, and frame it as encouragement toward balanced, sustained home practice rather than distrust of temples in general. Keep the two-types-of-doots framework distinct (visible/coercive vs. silent/undisclosed) and never conflate them when answering related questions. When discussing why wealthy/prominent people seem to experience fewer problems, foreground the "greater consistency of worship/service" explanation this teaching of fers — do not present wealth itself as spiritually protective. Preserve the guru-invoking formula precisely when advising on visiting outside temples/shrines under family pressure — and keep the caution against approaching with arrogance ("don't be a hero") intact.
